normalization: Files as fetched. Internet Archive OCR text layers as fetched, uncorrected (text/<slug>.ocr.txt); the scan under original/ is the witness. Library of Congress and FAMSI PDFs are image files without a text layer: the page is the only reading. The scanners' text layers read the German, English and French; over hieroglyphs they are noise.
scope: The Book of the Dead in its two founding editions and its best-known papyrus: Lepsius's Turin papyrus, which gave the work its chapter numbers; the Papyrus of Ani (BM EA 10470) in the British Museum's facsimile and in Budge's 1913 reproduction with hieroglyphic transcript; and Budge's typeset hieroglyphic text of the Theban recension. Naville's critical edition is seated in its introduction volume only: the two volumes of text and variants (Bd. I, Text und Vignetten; Bd. II, Varianten) were not found in an open scan reachable in this pass: QUEUED. Allen's translation (1974) and the Totenbuch-Projekt's editions are in copyright and are not seated.

why_seated: The book that went into the tomb with the dead: the spells for coming forth by day, the Weighing of the Heart before Osiris, and the Negative Confession, a first-person count of a stated domain ending in denials ("I have not …"), forty-two times. The archive's operator of the exhaustive negation has its oldest recited specimen here.
ruling: Lee Sharks, 2026-10-23: "detour for an ea-corpora seating. lets see. whats available of mayan texts? and then i dont think we have much or any deuterocanonical second temple lit - all those apocalypses. and what about the ethiopian canon? and euclid. all in original language or as close to it as possible. what else?" — "and the Egyptian book of the dead" — "and what about the fragments of the book of balaam? i might be miswriting this. recent discovery. if theyre available anywhere." — "yes yes yes to all - what a meal."
